annotations.text:
Circadia, two directions — pick one.

A · the dial — walks the six fields, promotes WHEN to the one dominant element; the back is a countdown over a 24h rail. Quiet, closest to what you have.
B · the composer — one command line that assembles as you click field chips; the back is a 7-day matrix of every armed fire. Denser, faster once learned, more to explain.

Both drop the permanent server rail. That rail is what made the old card feel heavy — it now lives on the back face.

Every two-faced card here flips for real — click the flip button.

Same 8-step horizontal squash as clip_ui.py (flip_width_scale, 16ms a step, faces swap at the midpoint).

The cabinet is the exception: it has no back, it has drawers.

This row is the legibility fix.

Storage face: each of the three products states its own preservation rule, its size, and its health — audio integrity, which transcription models the record was built from, how many readings are owed a recompute. The archive/shred toggle is the one destructive control, so it sits alone.

Cabinet: three drawers, one per store, one open at a time so the carcass never changes height. Click any row and the take highlights in all three drawers — the footer is the payoff line: one take, three products.
